Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

the next day adverb

also the day after, the following day, on the next day, the next morning, next morning, the day after that

classical

Caes. BC 1.67: prīmā lūce postrīdiē cōnstituunt proficīscī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 11.6.1: postrīdiē māne (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 86, 88
Traupman 300

postrīdiē

adverb; postrīdiē quam with a clause, postrīdiē ejus diēī, or with the accusative of a date

One word for “on the following day”; “the next morning” is postrīdiē māne or māne postrīdiē. The opposite is prīdiē.

Other words

  • posterō diē

    ablative of time · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.41: posterō diē māne (Lewis & Short s.v. posterus); Traupman 86; Traupman 300

Examples

  • invītat Canius postrīdiē familiārēs suōs, venit ipse mātūrē

    the next day Canius invites his friends, and comes early himselfCic. Off. 3.59

  • postrīdiē ejus diēī māne tripertītō mīlitēs equitēsque in expedītiōnem mīsit, ut eōs quī fūgerant persequerentur

    early the next morning he sent infantry and cavalry out in three columns on a campaign, to pursue those who had fledCaes. BG 5.10.1

  • māne postrīdiē

    the next morningTraupman 88

See also the day before, subsequent, tomorrow, the day after tomorrow.

SourcesLewis & Short: postridie · Lewis & Short: posterus
